purpose: Source manifest for the clinical guideline corpus. This repository ships NO guideline content. Download the documents you are licensed to use, place the PDFs in guidelines/pdfs/, then ingest them (see docs/guidelines-knowledge-base.md). This file is documentation for humans and is NOT read by the agent at runtime -- guidelines/catalog.json describes what is actually ingested locally.

licensing.public_domain: Works authored by US federal agencies (CDC, NHSN, NIH, NHLBI, NIAID) are in the public domain and may be redistributed freely.
licensing.link_only: Guidelines from professional societies (ADA, AHA/ACC/ASA, SCCM, ESICM, IDSA, ATS, KDIGO, BTF, NCS, AASM, AAFP, AAO-HNSF, AAP) are copyrighted. Most are free to read, but they may NOT be redistributed -- hence links rather than files. Note that free hosting on PubMed Central does not place a document in the public domain; copyright remains with the society. NICE (UK) guidelines are Crown/NICE copyright and free to download for individual use; they are indexed locally and cited by URL, never redistributed. EASL, ESUR and JBDS-IP guidelines are likewise copyrighted and free to download; indexed locally, cited by URL, never redistributed.
licensing.verification: Each entry records whether its URL was confirmed by direct retrieval. Major medical publishers and cdc.gov block automated clients with HTTP 403; entries marked verified=false were confirmed by an independent route (PubMed/Crossref for identity, Wayback Machine captures for .gov pages) and are recorded in verification_method. A 403 is a bot block, not a dead link.

coverage_note: The corpus deliberately spans critical care / emergency medicine alongside chronic disease and preventive care, because the reference dataset (MIMIC-IV) is an ICU/ED population. An earlier version of this corpus was weighted toward outpatient metabolic and cardiology content, which peer reviewers correctly identified as mismatched to ICU cases. Expanded 2026-08-21 (index guidelines-icu-baseline-v3): a trace audit of the 8-patient development cohort found the 18-source v2 corpus returned clinically off-target passages for 6 of 7 guideline searches, so sources covering the cohort's actual questions were promoted from this manifest (ADA Standards of Care, AHA/ACC chronic coronary disease, acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, hypertension) and two new entries added (atrial fibrillation, AASLD ascites/SBP). Where a society guideline proved unretrievable by any automated route (ahajournals.org and diabetesjournals.org sit behind a Cloudflare bot challenge that defeats browser headers, headless Chrome, Europe PMC -- the articles are inEPMC but not open-access -- and Wayback, whose captures of those URLs archive the challenge page itself), an equivalent NICE guideline covering the same clinical question was substituted so the corpus stays fully reproducible from public URLs. The unretrievable society entries are kept in this manifest as link-only provenance records with verified=false; they are not in the index.
